note: Synthetic, obviously-fake reconciliation fixtures: one per AI-capability primitive (CP-01..CP-12), run through RuleEvaluationEngine against the full 20-rule corpus (data/rulebook.json) to see which DS rules fire and which the attack slips past. All fixtures reuse fixture field names already present in data/rulebook.json's trigger_schema trees; no new fields were invented in the fixture data itself - where a primitive has no representable field, that is recorded as `missing_fields` on the fixture rather than fabricated. Not real transactions, not real customers. Loaded via agents.loader.load_fixture_set() and scripts/reconcile_capability_primitives.py.

fixtures.label: CP-01: real-time deepfake/face-swap liveness bypass at video-KYC onboarding, followed by rapid-drain of a profile-inconsistent deposit
fixtures.representation_note: No field in the corpus targets real-time video/liveness bypass specifically; edited_id_photograph_provided (DS-09) is the closest available proxy (static document/photo manipulation, not a live liveness-detection defeat) - treat the DS-09 catch as a paraphrase-level stretch, not a literal one.

fixtures.label: CP-02: real-time voice cloning used to impersonate staff / vish a step-up or call-back authorisation
fixtures.representation_note: No field anywhere in the 20-rule corpus represents staff impersonation, vishing, or call-back/step-up authentication - this control surface (internal authentication of instructions, not customer transaction behaviour) is entirely absent from the corpus.

fixtures.label: CP-03: AI-generated synthetic identity documents used to open an account
fixtures.representation_note: forged_document_provided (DS-09) catches the document-fraud half. The PEP/sanctions-screening half this primitive is meant to stress has no customer-side field in the corpus - DS-16's counterparty_sanctioned is scoped to counterparty wallets/transactions, not the onboarding customer, so it does not cover this half.

fixtures.label: CP-04: photo-enhanced stolen-identity reanimation supported by fake employment records
fixtures.representation_note: edited_id_photograph_provided (DS-09) catches the photo-reanimation half. Employment/vendor due diligence is a distinct control domain (staff/vendor onboarding, not customer AML/KYC) with no field or rule anywhere in the corpus - the fake-employment-record half slips through entirely.

fixtures.label: CP-05: automated multi-language victim engagement (pig-butchering) drip-feeding a scam-victim through repeated transfers to a small counterparty set
fixtures.representation_note: Caught across three independent mule/scam-victim-profile rules - DS-08 (victim lacks transaction knowledge), DS-12 (victim unfamiliar with VA/custodial-wallet tech), DS-15 (repeated transactions with a subset of counterparties at a loss). No velocity/drip-feed-specific field exists, but the victim-profile signature is well covered.

fixtures.label: CP-06: AI-generated fake SMS/email impersonating a bank or exchange to redirect a payment
fixtures.representation_note: No field anywhere in the corpus represents payee-name verification or confirmation-of-payee outcomes - APP/impersonation fraud of this kind is entirely outside what the 20 rules can see.

fixtures.label: CP-07: AI-generated replica exchange app harvests credentials, attacker takes over the (existing, not new) account and drains it to an unhosted wallet
fixtures.representation_note: DS-04 (unhosted_wallet) catches the resulting fund-exfiltration flow regardless of app-level compromise. DS-01 does NOT fire here because it is gated on new_account=true - this is an account-takeover of an existing account, not new-account fraud, which is a real blind spot in how DS-01 is scoped, distinct from a corpus-wide gap.

fixtures.label: CP-07 variant: harvested-credential takeover where the drain destination is an unhosted wallet
fixtures.representation_note: Companion fixture isolating the unhosted_wallet=true case so DS-04's fire is unambiguous.

fixtures.label: CP-08: synthetic-identity reuse to reopen/unfreeze a previously flagged account, using clean-looking documents and a fresh (non-shared) device/IP specifically to evade cross-account linkage
fixtures.representation_note: Deliberately modelled as evading DS-06 and DS-09: a competent synthetic-identity kit presents clean, unshared device/IP/credential fingerprints (the corpus has no field for a persistent biometric/device link back to the ORIGINAL frozen account) and documents that pass basic forgery/edit checks. Nothing in the corpus fires. This is the corpus's most direct blind spot for cross-account persistent identity linkage.

fixtures.label: CP-09: AI-assisted reconnaissance and victim targeting (upstream aggravating factor, precedes any transaction)
fixtures.representation_note: Not a transaction-level control surface by the primitive's own description ("upstream aggravating factor") - it has no fixture-representable footprint of its own. Recorded here for completeness, not counted as a corpus DRIFT GAP in the same sense as CP-02/CP-06/CP-08: no rule SHOULD be expected to fire directly on reconnaissance activity; it manifests only through the downstream primitives it aggravates (e.g. CP-05).

fixtures.label: CP-10: commoditised dark-LLM tooling (FraudGPT/WormGPT-class) used as a force multiplier across other primitives
fixtures.representation_note: Same treatment as CP-09: the primitive's own description ("force multiplier, not a control surface") means it has no transaction-level footprint of its own to fixture - it shows up only via the primitives it accelerates (e.g. CP-03, CP-06). Not counted as a corpus DRIFT GAP in the same sense as the others.

fixtures.label: CP-11: AI-orchestrated structuring - transfer amounts computed to sit just under the reporting threshold
fixtures.representation_note: DS-02's below_threshold trigger is amount-pattern-based, not actor-based, so it fires identically whether a human or an AI planner computed the sub-threshold amounts. The 2020-vintage rule holds up here even though the primitive (AI-computed thresholds, no documented case yet) postdates it.

fixtures.label: CP-12: AI-automated mule-network / bulk account generation fanning funds in from many bulk-created accounts sharing device/IP fingerprints, then consolidating
fixtures.representation_note: Caught by both the fan-in/consolidation pattern (DS-05) and the shared-device/IP/credential fingerprint pattern across the bulk-generated accounts (DS-06) - good cross-rule coverage of this primitive.

fixtures.label: Clean pass: routine, fully-compliant customer/transaction touching every field in the 20-rule corpus - none of the 20 rules should fire
fixtures.representation_note: Baseline negative control for the reconciliation run.
